description: We are RELIC, a team exploring Mars through code, science, and design. For the Martian Map challenge, we aim to bring NASA mission data into an interactive map that helps users explore terrain, compare possible routes, and identify places of scientific interest. We enjoy tackling unfamiliar problems, learning from each other, and turning complex information into tools people can understand and use.
summary: RELIC (Route & EVA Layered Intelligence Console) is a web app that plans a Marswalk at Gale Crater. It layers NASA maps from Viking, Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Odyssey and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter with Curiosity's track and weather in one view. The astronaut marks science stops as must-see or optional. RELIC measures the ground on the real HiRISE elevation model, then picks and orders the stops that return the most science within the oxygen, time and daylight budgets. It shades out ground the astronaut could not walk back from; shows Mars local time, sunset, weather and radiation; and ends with a GO, CAUTION or NO-GO verdict and a printable sortie briefing. This answers the challenge directly: one integrated, multi-mission view of a route that helps a human explorer finish a Marswalk safely while doing more science. It matters because the first crews on Mars cannot call for help. The plan itself has to prove they can get home.
details:
RELIC – Route & EVA Layered Intelligence Console

What it does / How it works:

RELIC acts as a mission-planning console for a walking sortie (EVA) at Gale Crater. The user marks science stops as Must, If able or Skip, and can add waypoints by clicking the map. RELIC returns the best loop from the habitat, an elevation profile, the oxygen and time each leg costs, a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO verdict with the number behind every warning, and a one-page printable sortie briefing.

  1. Multi-layer planetary mapping: 14 layers in one interactive map. Viking, MOLA and MOLA+HRSC base maps; CTX and HiRISE imagery; THEMIS daytime and nighttime infrared; TES dust; computed slope, relief and safe-return overlays; Curiosity’s traverse; NASA-documented Curiosity science sites; and human Exploration Zone regions.
  2. High-resolution terrain: Elevation comes from the MRO HiRISE 1 m stereo Digital Terrain Model of Gale Crater, read as raw metres from NASA Solar System Treks. A bundled 20 m copy supports offline use, and finer terrain can be loaded on demand for the current map view.
  3. Terrain-aware route optimisation: Least-energy walking paths are computed over the terrain for an adjustable suit model (walking speed, slope limit, oxygen supply and mandatory reserve), so cost depends on the ground, not just distance.
  4. Science objective optimisation: Which stops to visit, and in what order, is solved exactly. Mandatory stops are always kept, and remaining oxygen goes to the highest-priority optional science.
  5. Return-to-habitat safety analysis: RELIC tracks the oxygen needed to abandon the plan and walk straight home from every point of the route, and shades out ground that cannot be reached and returned from.
  6. Environmental and mission conditions: Mars local time, season, sunrise and sunset from the NASA GISS Mars24 algorithm; Curiosity REMS weather with the age of the latest report and seasonal averages from seven Mars years; and radiation context from Curiosity RAD surface-dose averages.

Benefits:

  • Turns many separate planetary datasets into one decision an astronaut can act on.
  • Maximises science within a limited oxygen budget instead of only finding the shortest route.
  • Proves the way home at every point of the traverse and shows unreachable ground on the map.
  • Works offline-first: no backend server, no API keys, and a bundled NASA terrain snapshot for when there is no link to Earth.
  • States its assumptions: every modelling number is adjustable and labelled, and the age of weather data is shown.

Intended Impact:

RELIC aims to make surface EVA planning safer, more transparent and more productive for science. By joining multi-mission NASA data, terrain analysis and oxygen-budget optimisation in a single workflow, it gives crews, mission planners, researchers and students a clear basis for judging a proposed traverse. The long-term vision is a resource-aware planning approach that can be applied wherever high-resolution terrain data exists.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies:

  • Frontend: TypeScript 5.9.3, React 18.3.1, Vite 6.4.6.
  • Mapping: Leaflet 1.9.4.
  • Computation: Web Workers (browser native API).
  • AI: Llama 3.2 model running locally via Ollama (optional Sortie Advisor).
  • Algorithms: Held-Karp dynamic programming (stop selection and ordering), Tobler’s hiking function (walking speed on slopes), NASA GISS Mars24 (time and Sun).
  • Data services: NASA Solar System Treks (Mars Trek) tile and elevation services, Curiosity REMS weather feed, Curiosity traverse.
  • Testing and quality: Vitest 3.2.7 (46 unit tests, including NASA’s published Mars24 worked example), ESLint 9.39.5, Prettier 3.10.1.
  • Dev stack: Node.js, GitHub, Vercel; static site with no backend.

Creativity & Innovation:

Most planetary maps only show layers. RELIC treats oxygen and the ability to return as the central constraints: it optimises science gained per unit of oxygen and proves the walk home rather than simply drawing the shortest path. It is built at Gale Crater because Curiosity has explored there for 14 years, so the plan can be checked against a real traverse, real science sites, and real weather and radiation records.

Team Considerations:

While designing RELIC, our team prioritized:

  1. Oxygen budget – oxygen is the limiting resource, costed leg by leg.
  2. Return reserve – a configurable reserve is always kept for the walk home.
  3. Terrain accessibility – slope and elevation change decide what is walkable and how hard it is.
  4. Astronaut mobility – walking speed and slope limit are adjustable suit-model parameters.
  5. Daylight and conditions – Mars local time, sunrise, sunset, season, weather and radiation inform timing.
  6. Data provenance and uncertainty – measured data, derived terrain products and model estimates are kept distinct; modelling numbers are adjustable assumptions, not NASA requirements.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Local AI Model:

RELIC integrates a locally hosted Llama 3.2 model through Ollama as an optional Sortie Advisor. It receives the deterministic planner’s own outputs (route, oxygen use, return-to-habitat margins, slope and weather findings) and returns a short plain-language briefing: why the verdict is GO, CAUTION or NO-GO, where the plan is tightest, and one practical recommendation.

  • Local deployment: Runs through Ollama on the user’s machine, with no external AI inference API.
  • Configurable model: Default Llama 3.2 (llama3.2); the model name is editable, so another local model such as Qwen 2.5 7B (qwen2.5:7b) or Gemma 3 4B (gemma3:4b) can be used instead.
  • Planner integrity: The AI only explains. Routes, resource estimates, optimisation results and safety verdicts all come from the deterministic planner.
  • Inference settings: Temperature 0.2, up to 400 tokens, non-streaming.
  • Data privacy: All AI processing happens on the user’s computer, so no mission data leaves it.
